text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need a compact set of playbook edits and a small set of triage scripts we can run from the on-call laptop. recurring pattern: overnight model load spikes -> 503s for ~3m. Can we split ownership and target a 2-week ship for the doc + scripts?

alex: Proposed action list (short):
1) Playbook: add exact escalation ladder + who to call at 0/2/10 minutes. owner: tess. due: 2024-12-09
2) Triage scripts: short shell checks + logs-to-keys. owner: sam. due: 2024-12-09
3) Deploy backstop: add fallback variant route for model-load failure. owner: alex. due: 2024-12-16
4) Scheduled warmup job: cron to pre-load model after deploys and at 23:50. owner: kevin. due: 2024-12-09
5) Post-deploy smoke: add `curl` health check and latency gate to CI. owner: tess + eng-sre. due: 2024-12-16

alex: For the triage script, here's the minimum set I want in `triage.sh` (1-liner checks + quick log grabs):
```sh
# quick health
curl -fsS https://redwood-infer.example/health || echo "health failed"
# backend model load latency stat (from metrics API)
curl -sS "https://metrics/api?query=model_load_latency_p50" | jq .
# grab recent runtime logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
```

alex: Also add an explicit escalation snippet for pager on-call: at 0m -> team channel, 2m -> eng-sre pager, 10m -> eng-platform on-call and manager. Put phone numbers/backup contacts into the playbook.

oncall-bot: Incident doc created: INC-2024-314 (linked in thread).

tess: I can take the playbook doc. I'll add the escalation ladder + make the checklist actionable with the exact commands. Will create a PR to `docs/playbooks/model-load-fallback.md`.

tess: Question — do we want the playbook to include the full `kubectl` commands or provide a one-click runbook script? I prefer both: the small script for on-call and the expanded steps for SREs.

sam: I'll own the `triage.sh` and the `logs-grab` helper. I'll add the metrics queries we need (p50/p95 model_load and request_error_rate). Will post the draft here when ready.

sam: Quick ask — for the metrics API endpoint, do we have a stable read-only token to include in the script, or should triage.sh prompt for `METRICS_KEY`?

alex: Put the token in the on-call vault / prompt is fine. Don't hardcode. Add a short note in the script that it reads `METRICS_KEY` from env or `gcloud secrets`.

kevin: I'll add the scheduled warmup job into infra as a Kubernetes CronJob. Proposed job: run 23:50 and 02:00 to pre-warm hot model state. I'll open infra PR and tag eng-platform.

kevin: Also, suggest we add a lightweight canary check post-deploy: run 5 requests with small prompt and assert 200 + mean latency < 300ms before opening the prod route. I can wire that into the deploy pipeline.

alex: Perfect. For tracking: I'll create the remediation epic in JIRA and link each owner. Please add the JIRA ID in your PRs. I'll hold reviews for the playbook PR until triage script and cronjob PRs are linked.

tess: SGTM. I'll start the doc now.

sam: On it — will post a first-pass `triage.sh` by EOD tomorrow.

kevin: Will try to have the cronjob PR by Friday.

alex: Thanks — once PRs are up, I'll run a short tabletop with on-call to walk through the commands and make sure they're usable under pages.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: tabletop runthrough set for 2024-12-05 16:00 UTC.

sam: noted.

kevin: noted.

alex: Closing note: keep playbook language prescriptive and minimum-steps-first. If anything needs to be escalated from docs->runbook, flag it.

sam: 👍

tess: :thumbsup:
